body:
sara (support): Heads-up — ACME Ops reported a large regression in p95/p99 after we promoted aurora-2-tokenv3 yesterday. They call it 'sudden slowdown' on long-context calls to /v1/generate (region=us-west-2). Their numbers: p95 ~1.2s (previous ~120ms), p99 ~3.8s for requests with ~34k tokens. Can we triage? :eyes:

ACME Ops (customer): Repro attached. Trace IDs: trc_0a1b2c3d, trc_0a1b2c3e. Example payload: ```POST /v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer sk_cust_XXXXX
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "model": "aurora-2-beta-tokenv3",
  "input": "<long prompt>",
  "max_tokens": 2048,
  "stream": false
}``` They said it only spikes when input tokens > ~30k.

Mike (runtime): Give me the trace IDs and I’ll pull logs. Also which host/shard they hit?

sara (support): Sent host: shard-usw2-07 in the support ticket.

Mike (runtime): Found the traces. Runtime log snippet for trc_0a1b2c3d:
```
[2026-03-15T08:14:22Z] trace=trc_0a1b2c3d latency_ms=3812 model=aurora-2-beta-tokenv3 step=tokenize details="bytes=32000 tokenizer=tokenv3 normalize=nfc"
[2026-03-15T08:14:22Z] trace=trc_0a1b2c3d latency_ms=3820 model=aurora-2-beta-tokenv3 step=forward batch=1
```
Tokenization is ~3.8s before forward. That’s the hot spot.

Jia (ml): tokenv3 introduced extra Unicode NFC normalization to fix some split-character bugs (esp. combining marks & emoji). On our nodes that path delegates to a Python shim that calls ICU via a non-vectorized codepath — worst-case O(N) per codepoint. For mixed CJK+emoji sequences this is expensive.

Eric (oncall): Was tokenv3 rolled out recently?

DeployBot: canary-deploy: aurora-2-beta-tokenv3 -> rollout 2026-03-14T18:02Z (canary=10%) promoted to 100% at 2026-03-14T20:55Z :rocket:

sara (support): ACME timeline matches the promotion window.

Jia (ml): I can implement a native C++ NFC path but ETA ~7d. Short term we should avoid routing long contexts to tokenv3.

Mike (runtime): Short-term options: rollback tokenizer to tokenv2, OR add routing rule to send requests with input_token_estimate > 16384 to aurora-2-tokenv2, OR add a safe fastpath that skips NFC when text looks ASCII-heavy. Routing rule is fastest — I can push in ~10m.

Eric (oncall): Push the routing rule. Set condition: input_tokens > 16384 -> model=aurora-2-tokenv2. Also create an alert for tokenization latency >500ms for 24–48h.

Mike (runtime): Creating the rule now.

DeployBot: routing-rule created id=rr_98765 by Mike. Rule: input_tokens>16384 -> model=aurora-2-tokenv2, scope=global, priority=50

AlertBot: incident created: INC-20260315-aurora-tokenize-longctx, severity=high, assigned=@Mike

sara (support): Notified ACME about the routing rule and offered a temporary model pin if they want to force the old tokenizer.

ACME Ops (customer): We tested ~30 minutes after the change. p95 ~130ms, p99 ~400ms. Much better. Still occasional spikes on mixed CJK+emoji messages.

Mike (runtime): Monitoring shows after rule: 2h p95 for aurora-2 dropped from 1.1s -> 140ms, p99 -> 480ms. Remaining spikes correspond to messages with mixed Unicode that still land on tokenv3 (edge cases where estimate misclassifies).

Jia (ml): Proposal for medium term: add ASCII-skew heuristic to skip NFC on inputs with <0.5% high-codepoint chars (PR within 48h), and implement native C++ normalization fallback (7d). Also add a tokenizer long-context micro-benchmark in onboarding CI.

Mike (runtime): Also a runtime improvement: tokenization currently happens per-request before batching. We should consider a prefix-hash stage that lets us reuse tokenization results across identical prefixes in a batch (avoids redoing N work). That's a 3–4 week RFC.

sara (support): Regarding billing — ACME noticed higher compute billed during the window. Recommend a small goodwill credit for requests where p99 > 2s during the regression window. Finance ok?

Eric (oncall): Approve small credit. Sara, coordinate with finance and CS to issue.

Jia (ml): Quick microbench: tokenv3 normalization ~0.12ms/char on ASCII, ~0.9ms/char for mixed CJK+emoji on our nodes due to fallback. At 30k chars that explains ~3–4s.

Mike (runtime): Repro snippet for ops/devs:
```
# produce long ASCII context
python -c "print('a '*40000)" > long.txt
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d @- https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate <<'JSON'
{"model":"aurora-2-beta-tokenv3","input":"`cat long.txt`","max_tokens":64}
JSON
```
Set TRACE_ID env to correlate logs.

Eric (oncall): Action items (owners):
- Mike: keep routing rule active, monitor 24–48h, alert for tokenization latency >500ms (DONE) ✅
- Jia: heuristic PR to skip NFC on ascii-heavy inputs (PR ~48h) ⏳
- Mike + infra: design batch-aware tokenization reuse (RFC) 📝
- Sara: follow up with ACME and close when stable ☎️

sara (support): I'll file the post-incident note and add onboarding checklist item: long-context tokenization perf for every tokenizer change.

Jia (ml): I'll add a tokenizer perf gate to onboarding CI (any change with O(N) impact needs a canary/limit).

Mike (runtime): Monitoring will keep an eye. I'll update the incident ticket with metrics after 24h.

sara (support): Customer happy with interim fix; keeping ticket open until 48h stable.

-- end of thread --
